title: bin/lore.cjs orphans the native child when the wrapper is killed: forward SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP and kill the child group (DEC-282 item 7, (a1))
description:
Filed by the lore-cli worker on the leader's dispatch for DEC-282 (a1). The quoted text below was read BY REF, not relayed: opum-doc dev 69af243cf42f56e4864cd093b37cb97f7ecd9bd6, .quest/planning.json, decisions[DEC-282].outcome.

VERBATIM, opum-doc DEC-282 item 7 and the (a1) paragraph it was ruled under:
"(a1) 2026-11-19, opum-doc, after the clock read 02:29:29Z, on cont1's follow-up over opum-comm (message 01a1f1a3-2a9a-7bad-ab3e-4d42bd6fde6a, at the operator's request). Not escalated. A live case on mbam5 at 02:24Z: the Mac's load was 41, with 4-9 concurrent `quest task list --across-refs --allow-partial --json` processes each running 60-90 s, many orphaned (PPID 1). The caller, a status daemon polling on a 500 ms watch and a 5 s tick with a 60 s timeout, killed only the node wrapper (quest.cjs), so the native quest binary kept running. The repository has 2,313 tasks and 47 worktrees of one clone."
"7. (new, a defect) The node wrapper must never orphan the native child. It forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to the child, and exits with the child's status. On the wrapper's own death the child must not outlive it: run it in its own process group and kill the group, or use an equivalent that leaves no orphan. Proof: a test that kills the wrapper mid-run and finds no surviving quest process. The same rule applies to lore's wrapper if it has one; lore-cli checks."

WHY THIS APPLIES TO THIS REPOSITORY. bin/lore.cjs is that wrapper. package.json's bin.lore points at it; it is the only file that runs under plain Node rather than Bun; its own docstring calls it the launcher; and its entire job is to resolve the platform package from optionalDependencies and exec the compiled binary with argv, stdio and exit code forwarded.

MEASURED read-only on 2026-11-19 by the lore-cli worker. Method: a byte-identical copy of bin/lore.cjs in a scratch directory (cmp-verified, regular file, not a symlink) with a stub platform package whose bin/lore writes its pid and execs a long sleep, driven by a node runner that spawns the wrapper through node and sends each signal to the WRAPPER's pid. POSITIVE CONTROL in the same run: killing the child directly flipped the liveness detector to false, so a "survived" answer cannot be a blind detector. RESULT: SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP each terminated the wrapper and the child was still alive 1.5 s later, in all three cases. The mechanism is visible in the source: the POSIX path is a single spawnSync with stdio inherit, which blocks the event loop, and the file registers no signal handler, so nothing relays a signal and nothing tears the child down on the way out. The Windows path (spawn with pipes) has the same gap and was not measured.

FIX SHAPE, NOT BUILT: give the child its own process group and forward SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to that group, killing the group on the wrapper's own exit, while leaving argv, stdio, exit-code and the 128+signal convention byte-identical for callers. The proof is a test that kills the wrapper mid-run and finds no surviving process for each of the three signals, which must go red when the forwarding is removed.

WHY THIS RECORD IS HOLD-LABELLED. DEC-182 (1) puts a change touching "the launcher" on the sensitivity floor: implementation at least Sonnet, security review on Opus, and no DeepSeek at any step, with "when unsure, treat it as sensitive". The lore-cli worker judges bin/lore.cjs to BE the launcher class, because it is the package's bin entry and it decides which binary runs. So a DeepSeek writer must not implement this. Reported to the leader on 2026-11-19; the leader routes it and lifts the hold. The dispatch prediction was "dispatch-floor lore-cli --paths bin/lore.cjs: CLEAR, floor none", and dispatch-floor is not installed in this session's PATH, so the judgement is recorded here in words rather than left to that tool.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test that kills bin/lore.cjs mid-run finds no surviving child process for SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP, and goes red when the forwarding is removed.
The wrapper forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to the native child and exits with the child status.
The child never outlives the wrapper: it runs in its own process group and the group is killed on the wrapper death, or an equivalent that leaves no orphan.

argv, stdio and the coded exit status are unchanged: the existing bin-lore and launcher-equivalence suites stay green. The 128+signal convention is SUPERSEDED by DEC-282 (a2) item 5: when the child dies of a signal the wrapper dies of the same signal, except SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1, which exit 128+signal.

implementationNotes: LEADER RULING, 2026-11-19: option A. bin/lore.cjs is treated as the DEC-182 (1) launcher class. It is the bin entry that decides which binary runs, and the rule is "when unsure, sensitive". It is built by a sonnet-or-higher lore-cli worker, with an opus security review, and no DeepSeek at any step. The hold stays, as filed. The leader arranges the routing (a sonnet-tier renewal); the DeepSeek worker that filed this record measured the defect and does not touch bin/lore.cjs. The fix shape and the measurement method recorded in the description above are where that build starts. When the sonnet build lands, the hold comes off.

Hold lifted 2026-11-19: the leader's brief to the sonnet-tier lore-cli successor (claude-sonnet-5-5) is the condition the hold waited for (option A, DEC-182 (1) launcher class: sonnet build, opus security review, no DeepSeek). launcher label kept. Design: stay in the wrapper's process group, forward SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the child, kill the child on wrapper exit (the AC's equivalent arm; detached would move the child out of the caller's group into a new session). Residuals to report: SIGKILL of the wrapper, Windows, repeated SIGINT on terminal Ctrl-C.

Delivered in this PR. Design: child stays in the wrapper's group; SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP forwarded; child SIGKILLed if the wrapper exits while it still runs; exit status = child's (128+n on signal). Evidence: test/bin-lore.test.ts new block, unpatched launcher 7 pass/3 fail (predicted, commit f448f180); patched 29 pass across bin-lore + launcher-equivalence; mutant with the forwarding removed gives exactly the 3 signal tests red and bin-lore/launcher-equivalence otherwise green. RESIDUALS: SIGKILL of the wrapper cannot be handled by any design; Windows path (spawn with pipes) unchanged and untestable here, process.kill SIGTERM on win32 is TerminateProcess (test is POSIX-only); a terminal Ctrl-C can deliver SIGINT twice to the child (tty signals the group, then the wrapper forwards). Possible divergence from quest-cli QCLI-567 on those axes.

REOPENED 2026-11-19 on the round-3 security review (B1), option (a): item 7 completes only with the lifeline (DEC-282 (a2) item 2), so this record stays In Progress and AC3 is unchecked. The implementation notes above this one describe the round-1 design (same group, exit 128+n) and are SUPERSEDED by this note.
DESIGN AS BUILT, DEC-282 (a2) items 1, 3 and 5, the same shape as quest's QCLI-567: off a TTY (stdin not a tty) the child is detached into its own session and group; TERM, INT and HUP go to the group (-pid); the wrapper SIGKILL-sweeps the group once, after the child closes and on the exit handler (swept at most once). On a TTY the child stays in the caller's foreground group and only the direct child is signalled. When the child dies of a signal the wrapper dies of the same one (listeners dropped, signal re-raised on itself) except SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1, where it exits 128+n; a synchronous spawn throw is reported as 'failed to run' with exit 1. Caller remedy documented: SIGTERM, wait a few seconds, SIGKILL.
AC4: its '128+signal convention' clause is SUPERSEDED by (a2) item 5 (death by the signal), so test/bin-lore.test.ts now asserts signalCode for that case; argv, stdio and the coded exit status are unchanged and their suites are green.
AC3 is completed by the carrier LCLI-799 (opum-ai/lore-cli#736): the lifeline pipe (item 2, kill -9 on the wrapper or the caller's group) and agent-plugins.ts:106 (item 4). Until then the residual is stated in CHANGELOG.md.

VERDICT: APPROVE
SHA: aaa64cd40

Scope: a read-only review with no shell. I read bin/lore.cjs, test/bin-lore.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md and .quest/tasks/LCLI-797.json at the head, plus the PR diff, the interdiff, the round-3 verdict, DEC-282 (a2)/(a3), and src/adapters/quest.ts:329-344. I ran no tests and re-measured no mutant. Mutant results are the writer's own claims.

FINDINGS
1. bin/lore.cjs:166 with src/adapters/quest.ts:332. NON-BLOCKING here, but it is a pair-wide design point for opum-doc. A nested quest native process can escape lore's sweep. lore spawns `quest` (the npm quest.cjs wrapper on PATH) with stdout and stderr piped. quest.cjs then finds no terminal, so it detaches its native child into its own session, which is outside lore's group. lore's sweep, kill(-lorepid, SIGKILL), reaches quest.cjs but not native quest.
   (a) Deterministic: on any path where lore's sweep hits quest.cjs before quest.cjs has forwarded, native quest is orphaned. Those paths are native lore killed by SIGKILL or OOM, and the exit-handler sweep after an uncaught exception.
   (b) A race in the incident shape: SIGTERM to the lore wrapper reaches quest.cjs at the same moment as native lore, and lore's close→sweep can SIGKILL quest.cjs before its JS handler forwards. A load of 41-128 widens that window.
   This contradicts (a2) item 1's "grandchildren (quest … under lore) die with it", and the docstring at :131 (ruling item 3), "A plain SIGTERM is fully handled". The code implements the ruling as written, and quest's lifeline closes the gap. Until then, CHANGELOG and the docstring should name it as a residual. I read this from the code and did not measure it.
2. .quest/tasks/LCLI-797.json, last implementationNote. NON-BLOCKING. "DESIGN AS BUILT" still says "off a TTY (stdin not a tty)". The note's updatedAt is 06:31:10Z and (a3) came after 06:43:40Z, so the record is stale against the three-fd rule. Fix it with --add-note, not --notes, which replaces the array.
3. .quest/tasks/LCLI-797.json, AC4. NON-BLOCKING. AC4 is still checked, and its text still says "including the 128+signal convention". Scored on its weakest clause it is not met; only the note explains the supersession.
4. .quest/tasks/LCLI-797.json. NON-BLOCKING. The note names the carrier LCLI-799 (#736), which does not exist at this SHA, and no structured field links to it. Confirm #736 actually carries that id, because ids can collide across branches.
5. test/bin-lore.test.ts:385. NON-BLOCKING, timing-dependent. Drop SIGUSR1 from NOT_RERAISED and the code and signal assertions are unchanged, because exitCode is set before the raise. Only `not.toContain("Debugger listening")` catches that mutant, and it depends on the inspector printing before the loop drains. It also misses if port 9229 is busy, because the failure message differs. A deterministic witness would be a kills.cjs-style preload asserting no SIGUSR1 sent to the wrapper's own pid.
6. test/bin-lore.test.ts:393. NON-BLOCKING. The SIGPIPE test passes against the round-3 code, and against a mutant that drops SIGPIPE (or SIGXFSZ) from NOT_RERAISED, since Node ignores both. It guards behaviour and does not witness the change; SIGXFSZ has no test at all. The exactly-once test at :402 is the real witness for N1: the round-3 code swept twice there.
7. test/bin-lore.test.ts:363-380. NON-BLOCKING, informational. Check 1 holds:
   - The stdin-piped/stdout-tty case is the fd 1 test, and fd 2 has its own witness.
   - Only the fd 1 and fd 2 cases go red under `!isatty(0)`. The fd 0 and "none" cases pass under both rules: they are regression guards, not (a3) witnesses.
   - The fd-0-only mutant is not in the tree; it exists only as the claim in 0b39cc56, which I did not re-measure.
   - The pgid > 0 guard and the fail-under-CI change close the vacuity concern.
8. test/bin-lore.test.ts:402. NON-BLOCKING, unverified. runLauncher does not pin stdin, while startLauncher does. If Bun.spawnSync inherits a terminal stdin on a local run, the wrapper takes the same-group branch, logs no negative-pid kill, and the test goes falsely red. This is not a vacuous pass. It is not a CI concern.
9. CHANGELOG.md:13. NIT. The 128+signal sentence sits inside the "Also not covered" list as if it were one of the uncovered items. Reads awkwardly.

CHECKS
- (a2), check 2. Clean: sweep runs before reraise (:199-200), a coded status passes through (:198), and listeners are dropped before the self-kill (:227-229). SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1 set exitCode to 128+n and drain; signal handles are unref'd, so nothing hangs.
- Item 7, check 3. With all three fds piped and SIGTERM to the wrapper, no surviving path within lore's own group:
  - A synchronous spawn throw, including ENOEXEC (or its sh fallback), is caught at :186-193 before any child exists.
  - An async spawn error leaves no pid.
  - An uncaught exception goes to the exit-handler sweep.
  - The sweep and the reraise are synchronous, so a second signal cannot interleave; after the listener drop, a later signal takes its default action with the group already swept.
  - In ownGroup mode, signalChild and sweep use process.kill inside try, so no 'error' event can bypass the sweep.
  - Theoretical, and only on the TTY branch: an EPERM from child.kill emits 'error' → failed() → exit with no sweep.
  - The cross-group escape is finding 1.
- Merge, check 5. Clean: four files only. CHANGELOG adds the single LCLI-797 bullet; dev's LCLI-791 and LCLI-718 bullets are intact, with no loss and no duplicate. No .quest/completed/LCLI-797.json duplicate exists.
- Record, check 4. Consistent with round-3 option (a): In Progress, AC3 unchecked, a superseding note. Findings 2-4 are the residue.

- N2: RESOLVED (NOT_RERAISED at :212). Its witness is timing-dependent (finding 5).

- N4: RESOLVED by the (a3) three-fd rule at :139, not tcgetpgrp. The CHANGELOG and docstring now state the direct-child-only limit.
- N5: RESOLVED (pgid > 0 at :350-351, and the CI no-skip at :362).
- N6: RESOLVED (forget(grandchildPid) at :275).

LEADER NOTE: #736's title at 9d8dbd477 is "chore(LCLI-799): file the carrier for DEC-282 (a2) items 2 and 4, tracker only", so finding 4's carrier id is confirmed by ref.

DESIGN AS BUILT, corrected for DEC-282 (a3) (review finding 2; the earlier DESIGN AS BUILT note said "off a TTY (stdin not a tty)" and is superseded on that point). The wrapper puts the child in its own session and process group ONLY when none of fds 0, 1 and 2 is a terminal (tty.isatty), which is every daemon and supervisor caller; when ANY of the three is a terminal the child stays in the caller's foreground group, so Ctrl-C, Ctrl-\, Ctrl-Z and /dev/tty prompts keep working, and there a signal sent to the wrapper alone reaches only the direct child. Everything else in the earlier note stands: TERM, INT and HUP forwarded to the group (-pid), one SIGKILL sweep of the group (at most once) after the child closes and in the exit handler, death by the child's signal except SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1 (exit 128+n), a synchronous spawn throw reported as 'failed to run' with exit 1. Landed in #734 as 99200bc8.

DEC-282 (a4) changes AC3 (the child never outlives the wrapper, kill -9 included): for the wrapper and native lore it still completes only with the lifeline (LCLI-799), and now also needs quest QCLI-571 for the nested native quest, which lore sweep cannot reach off a terminal. opum-ai/lore-cli#741 narrows the window (TERM-then-KILL exit sweep) and states the residual; it does not satisfy AC3. Read AC3 as: kill -9 on lore leaves no native lore AND no native quest, once both lifelines ship.
